firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
I know a few posts about this topic have already been made, but I wanted to share what I've been seeing and hopefully someone may have some advice for me.

So I tried running the Tufa Duck harness with qwen 3.8, and got local scores on the 25 public games of around 2.1%, with a public leaderboard score of around 1.4%. The public notebook shows a high score of 2.2% on the leaderboard. So I think the gap between 1.4% and 2.2% is likely just the randomness from the sampling.

I then tried out my own harness with qwen 3.8, and got local scores around 5.0-5.4%, but my public leaderboard score is still around 1.4%. I guess it's possible that I'm overfitting, but I don't have any game-specific directions for the 25 public games so I'm not sure where my overfitting could be coming from.

I understand that the public games are easier than the private games, but I would think that the drop between public and private would be relatively constant, right? So if Tufa goes from 2.1% -> 1.4%, then I would expect my harness that scores 5.4% locally to do much better than 1.4% on the leaderboard. 

I also understand that with the sampling mechanisms with qwen that some variance in score is expected, but I don't think sampling alone could explain the gap I'm seeing with my own harness. Is this just a case of overfitting, or is there potentially a submission bug in my code? Has anyone found any common bugs that could cause you to see larger gaps in public vs. private scores?
